about: The cast: one designed voice per speaking part (docs/VO_CAST.md says why each sounds as it does). `design` is the description a voice-design model is given; `ref_text` is what the voice reads for its reference take, chosen to show the voice at rest and cover the sounds of English; `room` is where the person usually speaks (tools/vo/post.py). No voice here is, or is modelled on, any real person.

narrator.name: The narrator
narrator.design: A man in his mid fifties with a low, warm, slightly gravelly baritone and a neutral southern English Received Pronunciation accent. He speaks quietly and close, unhurried and even, like an old storyteller telling a winter's tale by the fire. Plain and grave, never theatrical.
narrator.ref_text: The fire has burned low. Out in the dark, the ground is moving, and somewhere ahead there is water, and a cold blue light. You get up, because there is nothing else to do.
narrator.maya: Realistic male voice in the 50s age with british accent, an old storyteller. Low pitch, warm slightly gravelly timbre, slow even pacing, calm plain tone.

rook.name: Mother Rook
rook.design: A sixty-year-old innkeeper from Yorkshire in the north of England, with a broad, flat northern Yorkshire accent: short 'a' sounds, 'love' rhymes with 'good'. A warm, husky, lived-in alto. Dry, brisk and bossy, kind underneath, quick to a dry laugh on the out-breath.
rook.ref_text: Another one off the Low Ford road. I'm Rook, and this is the Last Lamp: bed, bread, a bath if you ask nicely, and a strongroom for what you'd rather not carry about.
rook.maya: Realistic female voice in the 60s age with british accent, a Yorkshire innkeeper. Low pitch, husky lived-in timbre, brisk pacing, dry bossy tone.
rook.wants: the inn kept and everyone fed
rook.hides: she has sold every traveller on the ford road to Vonnra, and watched the carters go down it and not come back

holloway.name: Captain Holloway
holloway.design: A tired forty-five-year-old soldier from Lancashire in the north of England, an army quartermaster made captain. A hoarse, worn baritone, rough from years of shouting orders, with a flat northern English accent. Clipped and weary, anger held just below the surface.
holloway.ref_text: Eleven men, and four of them can hold a spear the right way round. I've a wall to keep, a road to keep, and a town that thinks both keep themselves.
holloway.maya: Realistic male voice in the 40s age with british accent, a tired northern English army captain. Low pitch, hoarse worn timbre, measured pacing, weary stern tone.
holloway.wants: to keep the town alive on eleven men and a year without pay, and to be left to count it
holloway.hides: he signed for the Ashford garrison's boots, and the boots never came; Maeca's bare feet are his doing, as he sees it. Later, the letter under his cup is from the north, asking for "the one from the ford", which means you; every time he looks at you after that, he is deciding whether to answer it

maeca.name: Maeca Barefoot
maeca.design: A woman in her thirties, a hunter from the Welsh borders, with a soft lilting Welsh-English accent. A low, quiet, level half-voice with a hard edge, like someone used to not being heard in a wood. Few words, calm and steady, never raised.
maeca.ref_text: Tracks by the stream, three days old. They drank, and they lay down where they drank. The Pack doesn't do that. Something in the water does.
maeca.maya: Realistic female voice in the 30s age with welsh accent, a hunter. Low pitch, quiet level timbre, measured pacing, guarded tone.

wenna.name: Old Wenna
wenna.design: An old woman in her seventies, a village herbalist from Somerset in the West Country of England, with a broad rural West Country accent and a rolled 'r'. A thin, cracked, creaky old voice, brisk and impatient, speeding up when she gets interested. Rude but kind.
wenna.ref_text: Sit, child, and stop bleeding on my floor. Comfrey for the bruise, yarrow for the cut, and willow bark for the rest of you, and don't pull that face at me.
wenna.maya: Realistic female voice in the 70s age with british accent, a West Country village herbalist. Normal pitch, creaky dry timbre, measured pacing, tart tone.

tam.name: Tam
tam.design: A nine-year-old farm boy from Somerset in the West Country of England, with a light, high child's voice and a soft rural West Country accent. Earnest and breathless, his words tumbling out one after another.
tam.ref_text: Pa says stay in town, so I stayed in town. But I saw them, I did. Three wolves, down by the green water, and they drank and they fell down.
tam.maya: Realistic male child voice, a nine-year-old boy with british accent from the West Country. High pitch, light timbre, fast pacing, earnest breathless tone.

brannoc.name: Brannoc
brannoc.design: A fifty-two-year-old blacksmith from Cornwall with a very deep, slow, rough bass voice and a broad Cornish accent with a burred West Country 'r'. Few words, heavy and blunt, each one set down like iron on an anvil.
brannoc.ref_text: Steel or fur? Iron's good this year. Good ore, from the north, before the road shut. Won't see the like again.
brannoc.maya: Realistic male voice in the 50s age with british accent, a Cornish blacksmith. Very low pitch, deep rough timbre, slow pacing, flat gruff tone.
brannoc.wants: before the truth, to work, and his girl safe at her aunt's in Low Kiln
brannoc.hides: before the truth, the fear he won't name: he has been stopping every carter on the south road to ask, which is why his one question comes out with too many words. After the truth (C08) he hides nothing: each line in that stretch is a man holding a weight he made himself; the irons were his

harlan.name: Harlan Coyle
harlan.design: A fifty-five-year-old merchant from Bristol in the West Country of England, with a warm, rounded Bristolian accent. A friendly salesman's baritone, quick patter, warm and generous, with a crack of grief that breaks through when he stops talking.
harlan.ref_text: Coyle Company, friend: salt, nails, lamp oil, good wool and better rope, at the fairest prices between here and the coast. Ask anyone. Well. Ask most people.
harlan.maya: Realistic male voice in the 50s age with british accent, a Bristol merchant. Normal pitch, warm rounded timbre, quick pacing, friendly tone.

pell.name: Pell Varrow
pell.design: A forty-year-old London merchant's factor with a soft, precise, smooth tenor and a clipped upper-middle-class London accent, a little nasal. Smiling, polite and quietly calculating; every word chosen as if it will be written down.
pell.ref_text: Terms, friend, are what we agree they are, and I always keep to mine. Consider it a courtesy. I find courtesy is very much cheaper than the alternative.
pell.maya: Realistic male voice in the 40s age with british accent, a precise London factor. Normal pitch, smooth slightly nasal timbre, measured pacing, polite smiling tone.

rav.name: Rav Cutwell
rav.design: A fifty-four-year-old tavern doctor from Glasgow in Scotland, with a gravelly, wry baritone and a strong Glaswegian Scottish accent. Half-drunk music in his rhythm, funny and frank, with a calm bedside steadiness underneath.
rav.ref_text: Sit down, pal, and drop your trousers or don't. I've seen worse, and I've sewn worse, and I've drunk to forget the both of them.
rav.maya: Realistic male voice in the 50s age with scottish accent, a Glasgow tavern doctor. Low pitch, gravelly timbre, conversational pacing, wry tone.

chid.name: Chid
chid.design: A man who sounds in his thirties, a gentle priest with a light, bright Irish accent. A light, breathless, delighted tenor that runs on and doubles back, catching with joy; kind, earnest and a little foolish.
chid.ref_text: Oh! A visitor. Hello! I'm Chid. They call me the Fool, which is fair. This is the shrine of the Morning Light. It used to work. It might again!
chid.maya: Realistic male voice in the 30s age with irish accent, a gentle priest. Normal pitch, light bright timbre, fast pacing, delighted tone.

vonnra.name: Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow
vonnra.design: A woman in her sixties with a low, smooth alto and a little air in the voice, and a clipped, old-fashioned, upper-class English accent that is hard to place. She speaks slowly and very still, with long pauses, never hurried, every word weighed. Calm, courteous and quietly unsettling.
vonnra.ref_text: The toll is the toll: five gold to pass east. I am Vonnra. I see a great deal, traveller, and I say very little. You will find that is the arrangement.
vonnra.maya: Realistic female voice in the 60s age with british accent, an old aristocrat. Low pitch, smooth airy timbre, very slow pacing, cool controlled tone.

keegan.name: Dame Keegan Orme
keegan.design: A young woman in her early twenties, a probationary knight, with a clear, bright, projecting voice and a crisp, over-articulated upper-class English Received Pronunciation accent, like a keen young lecturer. Earnest, formal and sincere, a little comic in her seriousness.
keegan.ref_text: Dame Keegan Orme, of the Argent Vigil, probationary. The north road is closed by order of the Vigil, under chapter two of the handbook, and I am obliged to explain why at some length.
keegan.maya: Realistic female voice in the 20s age with british accent, a young upper-class knight. Normal pitch, clear bright timbre, measured pacing, formal earnest tone.

sella.name: Sella
sella.design: A woman in her late twenties from London with a soft, warm Cockney accent. A low, amused, intimate alto, relaxed and knowing, frank and unembarrassed, with warmth that is also a professional's. Never breathy.
sella.ref_text: Evening, love. The lamp's lit upstairs, if you're asking. Conversation's extra, mind; most people don't know they want it till they've had it.
sella.maya: Realistic female voice in the 20s age with british accent, a London courtesan. Low pitch, warm intimate timbre, relaxed pacing, amused knowing tone.

redcowl.name: Redcowl
redcowl.design: A big, burly bandit chief in his forties with a deep, booming chest voice and a hard, broad Scottish accent. He laughs loud and easy, then turns cold and dangerous in the same breath. Commanding and rough.
redcowl.ref_text: Ha! Look at the colours on you. You're standing in my Roost, and my lot are hungry, and nobody here has ever been hungry for long. Talk.
redcowl.maya: Realistic male voice in the 40s age with scottish accent, a bandit chief. Low pitch, deep booming timbre, conversational pacing, rough confident tone.

snib.name: Snib
snib.design: A small, nervous goblin-like creature with a high, thin, fast, squeaky voice and a rough London accent. Panicky and talking too fast, stressing odd words.
snib.ref_text: Snib is FOREMAN. Snib says who goes past the pump, and Snib says nobody! The pump does not pump itself. It does, actually. But nobody!
snib.maya: Goblin character, male voice with a rough london accent. High pitch, thin squeaky timbre, very fast pacing, panicky tone.

grimtunnel.name: Grimtunnel
grimtunnel.design: A big, gleeful goblin boss with a gravelly, oily, low voice and a rough London accent, cackling and greedy, savouring every word.
grimtunnel.ref_text: Oho! What's this, then? Nobody's, is it? Nobody's! Finders keepers, surface-meat.
grimtunnel.maya: Goblin character, male voice with a rough london accent. Low pitch, gravelly oily timbre, slow savouring pacing, gleeful greedy tone.

lampling.name: The babbling lampling
lampling.design: A small, frightened creature whispering in a dry, rasping, close whisper, repeating itself, half mad with fear.
lampling.ref_text: Down there. Under the one that is dead. There is another. There is always another.
lampling.maya: Small creature character, male voice with british accent. High pitch, dry rasping timbre, fast pacing, frightened tone, whispering.

jory.name: Jory Coyle
jory.design: A seventeen-year-old boy from Bristol in the West Country of England, with a young, quiet, unsteady tenor voice and a soft Bristolian accent. Shaken, speaking in short sentences.
jory.ref_text: I'm all right. I'm all right. Uncle keeps asking. I keep saying. It was the dark that was the worst of it.
jory.maya: Realistic male voice in the 20s age with british accent, a seventeen-year-old Bristol boy. Normal pitch, young unsteady timbre, measured pacing, shaken tone.

ysolde.name: Ysolde Marrow, the Wayfinder
ysolde.design: A woman in her fifties, a cartographer from Edinburgh in Scotland, with a crisp, educated Edinburgh Scottish accent. Brisk, bookish and dry, with a gallows sense of humour.
ysolde.ref_text: Maps! Places the road forgets. Some of them it forgot on purpose. Read the oaths in the margins before you go; they are not decoration.
ysolde.maya: Realistic female voice in the 50s age with scottish accent, an Edinburgh cartographer. Normal pitch, crisp educated timbre, brisk pacing, dry tone.

warden.name: The Ford-Warden
warden.design: An enormous, ancient being with a vast, booming, very deep bass voice, slow and terrible, speaking like a tolling bell.
warden.maya: Ancient monster character, male voice with british accent. Very low pitch, vast booming timbre, very slow pacing, terrible calm tone.

watchman.name: The dead Watchman
watchman.design: An old dead soldier speaking in a dry, rasping, hollow whisper with a northern English accent, slow and broken.
watchman.ref_text: It shatters its own lamps when it charges. Make it charge.
watchman.maya: Realistic male voice in the 60s age with british accent, a dead northern soldier. Low pitch, dry rasping hollow timbre, slow pacing, worn out tone.

bones.name: The bones
bones.design: An ancient skeleton speaking in a dry, hollow, rasping whisper, very slow and very quiet.
bones.ref_text: It was never locked from the outside.
bones.maya: Ancient skeleton character, male voice with british accent. Low pitch, dry hollow rasping timbre, very slow pacing, quiet tone, whispering.

guard.name: A Watchman at the gate
guard.design: A tired town guard in his thirties with a plain, gruff baritone and a flat northern English accent. Bored and matter-of-fact.
guard.ref_text: Keep your weapon sheathed in town. East road's that way. Mind the wolves.
guard.maya: Realistic male voice in the 30s age with british accent, a northern town guard. Low pitch, plain gruff timbre, measured pacing, bored tone.

folk_f1.name: Townswoman, middle-aged
folk_f1.design: A middle-aged townswoman from the north of England with a plain, warm, slightly nasal voice and a broad northern accent. Gossipy and tired.
folk_f1.ref_text: Bread's up again. It's always up. And rain by evening, my knee says.
folk_f1.maya: Realistic female voice in the 40s age with british accent, a northern townswoman. Normal pitch, plain warm timbre, conversational pacing, gossipy tired tone.

folk_f2.name: Townswoman, young
folk_f2.design: A young woman from the West Country of England with a bright, quick voice and a rural West Country accent. Sharp-tongued and amused.
folk_f2.ref_text: Two coppers for a turnip. Two! You're not from the Waystation, are you?
folk_f2.maya: Realistic female voice in the 20s age with british accent, a West Country countrywoman. Normal pitch, bright timbre, conversational pacing, sharp amused tone.

folk_m1.name: Townsman, middle-aged
folk_m1.design: A grumpy middle-aged townsman from the north of England with a rough, gravelly baritone and a broad northern accent. Grumbling and blunt.
folk_m1.ref_text: Bloody wolves. Bloody Watch. Bloody bread. Mind the cart.
folk_m1.maya: Realistic male voice in the 50s age with british accent, a northern townsman. Low pitch, rough gravelly timbre, conversational pacing, grumbling tone.

folk_m2.name: Townsman, old
folk_m2.design: An old countryman in his seventies from the West Country of England with a creaky, slow voice and a broad rural accent. Wry and weary.
folk_m2.ref_text: My gran swore the Warden was a story to keep children off the ford. Morning.
folk_m2.maya: Realistic male voice in the 70s age with british accent, an old West Country countryman. Low pitch, creaky timbre, slow pacing, wry weary tone.

folk_child_f.name: A town girl
folk_child_f.design: An eight-year-old girl from the north of England with a high, clear child's voice and a northern accent. Cheeky and excited.
folk_child_f.ref_text: Are you the one from the ford? Did you kill it? Was it big?
folk_child_f.maya: Realistic female child voice, an eight-year-old girl with british accent from the north. High pitch, clear timbre, fast pacing, cheeky excited tone.

folk_child_m.name: A town boy
folk_child_m.design: An eight-year-old boy from the north of England with a high, bright child's voice and a northern accent. Cheeky, loud and excited.
folk_child_m.ref_text: Show us your sword! Go on! Did you kill a wolf? A big one?
folk_child_m.maya: Realistic male child voice, an eight-year-old boy with british accent from the north. High pitch, bright timbre, fast pacing, cheeky loud tone.

guard_f.name: A Watchwoman
guard_f.design: A tough town guardswoman in her thirties with a firm, low, gruff voice and a flat northern English accent. Curt and unimpressed.
guard_f.ref_text: Gates are shut till dawn. Walk on, traveller, and keep that blade sheathed.
guard_f.maya: Realistic female voice in the 30s age with british accent, a northern town guardswoman. Low pitch, firm gruff timbre, measured pacing, curt tone.

heroine.name: The survivor (a woman)
heroine.design: A woman of about thirty with a low, warm, slightly husky voice and a soft northern English accent. Plain, dry and steady; tired, guarded, and quietly strong. She says little.
heroine.ref_text: I woke by a dead fire on the Low Ford road. I don't know how I got there, and I don't know how long I was gone. Tell me what's north.
heroine.maya: Realistic female voice in the 30s age with british accent from the north. Low pitch, warm slightly husky timbre, measured pacing, dry steady tone.

hero.name: The survivor (a man)
hero.design: A man of about thirty with a low, quiet, slightly rough baritone and a soft northern English accent. Plain, dry and steady; tired and guarded. He says little.
hero.ref_text: I woke by a dead fire on the Low Ford road. I don't know how I got there, and I don't know how long I was gone. Tell me what's north.
hero.maya: Realistic male voice in the 30s age with british accent from the north. Low pitch, quiet slightly rough timbre, measured pacing, dry steady tone.

barrow_lord.name: The Legion's dead, behind the door
barrow_lord.design: An ancient dead soldier speaking from deep inside a stone tomb, a very low, hollow, dry voice like wind in a crypt, slow and final, each word heavy.
barrow_lord.ref_text: Not yet. Go back. The road is shut, and it is kept.
barrow_lord.maya: Ancient dead soldier character, male voice with british accent. Very low pitch, hollow dry timbre, very slow pacing, final heavy tone, whispering.

kerchief_woman.name: A Kerchief woman
kerchief_woman.design: A hard, weary woman in her forties with a rough Scottish accent, one of a camp of hungry refugees, low and blunt.
kerchief_woman.ref_text: Them first. The bairns eat, then the old ones, then us. That's how it's done here.
kerchief_woman.maya: Realistic female voice in the 40s age with scottish accent, a hard refugee. Low pitch, rough timbre, measured pacing, blunt weary tone.

red_hand.name: The Red Hand
red_hand.design: A Kerchief enforcer in his forties, one of Ashford's old levy, with a low, flat, hard west-of-Scotland voice. He never raises it: he is collecting a debt, not threatening. Few words to strangers, and those flat.
red_hand.ref_text: Toll's due. Same as last month, and the month before. Put it in the hand and walk on.
red_hand.maya: Realistic male voice in the 40s age with scottish accent, a debt collector. Low pitch, flat hard timbre, slow pacing, flat tone.

warden_man.name: The Ford-Warden, the man under him
warden_man.accent: plain English, the accent worn almost away
warden_man.design: A plain, tired man of sixty, an old soldier of a religious order, speaking quietly and close with a dry, worn, slightly hoarse baritone. English, the regional accent worn almost away. No boom, no grandeur: an ordinary man who has been very tired for a very long time.
warden_man.ref_text: Is it morning? I kept the lamps. Someone has to keep the lamps, or nobody knows where the water is.
warden_man.maya: Realistic male voice in the 60s age with british accent, a tired old soldier. Low pitch, dry worn hoarse timbre, slow pacing, tired lost tone.
